name: LA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Deep-blue district with a 25-point Democratic partisan lean
Incumbent Troy Carter running with a large fundraising edge
Prediction markets price Carter at 98% to win

model.rationale: Carter holds a heavily Democratic New Orleans-based seat, has raised $1.4 million against a little-known Republican with no reported fundraising, and markets give him a 98% chance. The fundamentals point to a blowout, so the forecast stays at a roughly 27-point Democratic margin.
model.watch: A surprise primary-style upset or an unexpectedly competitive runoff dynamic is the only realistic path to changing this call.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Louisiana's 2nd District is one of the most Democratic-leaning seats in the country, anchored in New Orleans, with a partisan lean of about 25 points toward Democrats. Incumbent Troy Carter is running for another term and enters with a clear financial advantage, having raised about $1.4 million, while Republican Peter Williams shows no reported fundraising or outside spending.

No general-election polls or expert ratings exist for the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money. Prediction markets price Carter's chances at roughly 98 percent. All available evidence points to a comfortable Democratic hold, with the main question being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
